intro: Clinical research coordinators organize studies, work with patients and keep data accurate, skills used in data management and health education. The closest of the 25 careers below is Clinical Data Managers, with an 85% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $120,230 for its broader group.
why_it_works: Running a trial means recruiting participants, following strict protocols and keeping records ready for audits. O*NET rates coordination at 3.88 out of 5 for this job, and complex problem solving, judgment and social perceptiveness at 3.62. Data management, research and claims work use the same accuracy. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Clinical data management is the closest move and pays well; learn the data systems your sponsors use.
Health Informatics Specialists are a 75% match with a median of $105,850, though many need a graduate degree.
Claims adjusters and examiners are a 76% match if you want to stay close to medical records.

faq.q: What jobs can former clinical research coordinators do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Clinical Data Managers (85%), social science research assistants (84%) and Health Education Specialists (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Claims adjusters, examiners and investigators are 76% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $78,000.

faq.q: Which jobs for clinical research coordinators pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Clinical Data Managers at $120,230, postsecondary health specialties teachers at $107,310 and Health Informatics Specialists at $105,850, according to BLS May 2025 data. Teaching and informatics often require a graduate degree, while data management usually does not.

faq.q: Do clinical research coordinators need another degree?
faq.a: For most paths, no. 21 of the 25 matches need no more education than research coordinators already have, including 7 of the top 10, while 4 usually need a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 85% of workers in the closest match.

faq.q: What skills should clinical research coordinators learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are operations analysis, programming, quality control analysis and operation and control. Judgment already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so data and programming skills are the main step toward data management.
